status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified

status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified

status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified

title: How common is a reported net gain at each age?
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: 2023-24. Denominator is tax filers in each age group, not all residents or asset holders.

status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified

status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: 2023-24. Means are not medians; recorded sex follows ATO disclosure categories. Composition and asset ownership are not controlled for.

title: Concentration across taxable-income percentiles
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: 2023-24. Taxable filers only; this is income-ranked concentration, not a wealth Lorenz curve. Annual gains affect the ranking.

title: Capital income extends well beyond taxable capital gains
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: 2023-24. Gross interest/rent and dividend components versus net taxable gains: this is a reported-income map, not an economically consistent net capital-income total.

title: Many small gains, a large share of dollars in large gains
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: 2023-24, all taxable statuses. Net gain ranges refer to after-loss/discount amounts, not sale proceeds.

title: Estimated tax relative to net taxable gains
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: ATO estimated tax allocation, not cash collected; denominator is already net of discounts/losses. This is not an effective rate on gross economic gains.

title: A longer history of individuals’ net taxable gains
status: ATO observations, approximately CPI-deflated into 2023-24 purchasing power
note: Net taxable gains reflect successive tax rules and reporting changes, including the 1999 discount. This history does not identify the causal effect of reform.
sources: ATO Individuals Table 1A; ABS CPI via RBA G1

title: Rental income, borrowing costs and other deductions
status: Observed Australian tax-return data; income years end in June; nominal AUD unless specified
note: Rental-property schedule coverage; not unique landlords. Other deductions include capital works/depreciation. Not a measure of real economic profit.

title: Who receives the measured benefit of the CGT discount?
status: Treasury TEIS distributional estimate for 2022-23; pre-reform benchmark
note: Income decile includes gains. A tax expenditure is benchmark-dependent revenue forgone, not the revenue obtainable from repeal. Published shares are rounded.

title: Age profile of the existing discount’s estimated benefit
status: Treasury TEIS distributional estimate for 2022-23; pre-reform benchmark
note: Shares and recipient numbers are distinct; this does not measure a lifetime distribution of reform burdens.

title: CGT receipts in the 2026-27 Budget
status: Published conditional Budget/PBO estimates; source vintages are kept separate
note: 2024-25 actual; subsequent years are Budget estimates. CGT is embedded in individual/trust, company and superannuation taxes, not an additional tax line.

title: How large is CGT relative to all Commonwealth tax receipts?
status: Published conditional Budget/PBO estimates; source vintages are kept separate
note: Same cash-receipts denominator and Budget vintage; not CGT divided by personal income tax.

title: The combined CGT and negative-gearing Budget costing
status: Published conditional Budget/PBO estimates; source vintages are kept separate
note: Not a stand-alone CGT score. Budget announcement vintage; dash and .. rendered as zero (.. is rounded small magnitude). No new behavioural adjustment is applied.

title: Reform receipts build beyond the forward estimates
status: Published conditional Budget/PBO estimates; source vintages are kept separate
note: July 2026 PBO preliminary medium-term estimates, rounded to $0.1bn. CGT and negative gearing are combined. These are not updated November legislative costings.

title: Cumulative medium-term amounts depend on the chosen window
status: Published conditional Budget/PBO estimates; source vintages are kept separate
note: Sum of rounded PBO annual estimates. A cumulative amount is not an annual permanent yield.

title: The benchmark matters: CGT-related tax expenditures
status: Treasury December 2025 TEIS estimates; pre-Budget policy baseline
note: Separate main-residence benchmark components and discount estimate. Do not add as repeal revenue or compare directly with the combined reform score.

title: Inflation, the normal return, and excess returns are separate
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $100k principal; inflation 2.5%, real normal return 3%, excess real return 4pp. Uses exact nominal compounding, not simple addition.

title: How much future consumption can the same new earnings buy?
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $100k pre-tax new labour resource; 30% income-inclusive rate and matching 42.86% consumption-tax rate. Normal real return 3%, inflation 2.5%. RRA and consumption lines coincide.

title: An allowance removes the tax wedge between consuming now and later
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Normal-return-only case. Consumption measured after tax. Does not assert identical distribution, treatment of existing wealth, or all risky outcomes under actual GST.

title: Matching income-inclusive and GST-style tax-exclusive rates
status: Algebraic mapping, not a proposed GST rate
note: s = t / (1 - t). Australian GST is 10%; a 30% income tax is not equivalent to a 30% GST.

title: RRA and cash-flow taxation: an exact present-value comparison
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: New $100k investment, 10 years, 30% flat tax. Discount at the 5.575% nominal allowance rate. Full immediate-value loss relief; RRA and cash-flow lines coincide. Risk would require state pricing.

title: CPI indexation protects principal; a normal allowance protects more
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $100k cost, no interim payouts. CPI 2.5%; nominal normal allowance 5.575%. Basis growth is not a cash subsidy or observed return.

title: Same total return, different split between payouts and gains
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Total nominal return 8%; 30% flat tax, no leverage or company tax. Gain leg is assumed eligible for discount/indexation. Stylised annual-equivalent comparison; exact holding dates not modelled.

title: Choosing the allowance rate changes what is taxable
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: One-period real-dollar arithmetic on $100k at 30%. A risk-free allowance is distinct from exempting each investor’s expected risky return. Negative tax assumes fully usable relief.

title: Unused allowances need a time-value rule
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: All return paid as terminal appreciation. Simple addition of unused annual allowances fails to preserve the compounded normal basis.

title: The effective tax rate on real gains depends on the return
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $500k asset, 10 years, $70k other annual taxable income, CPI 2.5%. Frozen 2027-28 basic tax; Medicare and offsets omitted. Rates above 200% clipped visually; CSV retains them.

title: Tax dollars: inflation adjustment and the minimum rate do different jobs
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Fresh $500k eligible asset, 10 years, CPI 2.5%, $70k other income. These are basic-tax illustrations, not full tax-return calculations.

title: When does the reform raise or reduce tax in the illustration?
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Difference: indexed/minimum tax minus old discount. $500k initial cost, CPI 2.5%, $70k other income. Only new-regime accruals, no grandfathered gains.

title: Holding period and other income both matter
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Fresh $500k asset growing 6% nominal; CPI 2.5%; other income fixed at sale. No claim about actual distribution of holding periods.

title: The minimum tax is a top-up to basic tax, with specified exemptions
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Frozen 2027-28 resident scale. 30% floor on eligible gain before offsets; no Medicare. Exemption illustrated as a legal status, not a prediction of benefit eligibility.

title: Progressive-tax bunching is separate from the value of deferral
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $15k real annual gain, constant-dollar frozen thresholds; CPI already removed. No discounting here: isolates progressive bunching. Averaging is a counterfactual, not enacted policy.

title: Transition: gains before and after July 2027 need separate treatment
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $500k original cost, 6% nominal appreciation, CPI 2.5%, other income $70k. Supplied market valuation; no losses, trusts or alternative Commissioner apportionment. Not a complete implementation calculator.

title: Deferral changes terminal wealth even when gains are fully taxed
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $100k already-taxed principal; 5% real return; 30% flat tax; 3% real RRA; no inflation, company tax or credit constraints in this real-dollar model. Half-rate comparator is not the nominal Australian discount.

title: Deferral expressed as an annual after-tax return
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Same real-dollar flat-tax assumptions as R01. At exactly the RRA normal return, RRA tax is zero. No empirical investor-return forecast.

title: How much better must a replacement investment be to justify sale?
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Current asset earns 5% real; 30% full real CGT. Sale taxes embedded gain, reducing reinvestable funds; both paths liquidated after 10 years. No transaction costs.

title: A future loss deduction is worth less than immediate relief
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $10k loss at 30% tax. Certain eventual use is assumed; expiry or never realising an offsetting gain would reduce value further.

title: Taxing gains and sharing losses have different risk effects
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Success +$200k, failure -$100k, flat 30% tax. Restored scale multiplies investment by 1/(1-t). Requires finance and fully symmetric relief; not an actual CGT loss rule.

title: Risk evaluation depends on the loss rule and the investor
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Illustrative log utility, $300k initial wealth, unscaled +$200k/-$100k project. Not estimated preferences, probabilities or welfare effects.

title: Leverage interacts with deductions and the definition of taxable return
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $500k asset, growth 4%, rent net of non-interest costs 2.5%, borrowing 6.5%, flat tax 30%. Immediate relief on negative net taxable income is assumed; eligible longer-held gain treated at annual equivalent.

title: Indexing gains raises a parallel question about interest deductions
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $500k asset; inflation compensation on nominal debt principal; 30% flat tax. A comprehensive real-income system also adjusts lenders’ interest receipts. This is not a costing.

title: Company tax cannot simply be added to personal tax on dividends
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: One period, immediate full distribution and fully usable/refundable credits. No claim that credits are fully capitalised in share prices, or all shareholders receive them. Retained gains need a fuller model.

title: Matching saving incentives does not make transition burdens identical
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: 3% normal real return. Hypothetical new comprehensive consumption tax at 42.86%, without compensation, versus 30% labour tax + RRA. Existing GST and transition compensation are not modelled.

title: CPI indexation need not give symmetric relief for real losses
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: $100k cost, CPI 2.5%, flat tax 30%. Indexation does not create/increase a nominal capital loss. Assumed future capital-loss use is discounted at 5.575%; no cash refund is promised by CGT.

title: Some apparent capital gains can embody the owner’s own work
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Stylised fixer-upper: $500k purchase plus $50k cash improvements at inception, held 2 years, 6% growth, work adds $60/hour to sale value. Unpaid own work has no recorded cost deduction. Abstract CGT case; excludes main-residence/trading rules.

title: Published behavioural numbers use different definitions
status: Original-author/official-costing parameters; ranges show specifications, not confidence intervals
note: Canada WP2021 ranges shown without point estimates. OBR uses scoring assumptions. Do not pool these into a single Australian elasticity. Native reference rates and caveats are in the CSV.

title: Converting to a tax-rate elasticity still requires a reference rate
status: Definition conversion, not harmonised identification or an Australian calibration
note: e_tax = beta*t for semi-log; e_tax = -e_net*t/(1-t). OBR conversion rates are illustrative; these are not equivalent estimands.

title: The same local elasticity gives different responses to large tax changes
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Constant semi-elasticity and constant net-of-tax forms match locally at 22%, then diverge. Assumed parameters, not a simulation of the Australian base/indexation reforms.

title: Revenue curves depend on the behavioural model
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Gains base starts at index 100. Peaks are functional-form illustrations, not estimates of Australia’s revenue-maximising or welfare-maximising rate.

title: How much of a static revenue increase survives a response?
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Finite increases under constant semi-elasticity. The shortcut 1+elasticity applies only locally. Does not adjust published Budget costings, which already incorporate Treasury judgements.

title: A surge before a tax change can be followed by a slump
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: Pure timing illustration shifts 30 units into year -1 and removes 10 in each of years 0-2. Total gains conserved over the full window; no permanent response assumed.

title: Fewer reported capital gains need not mean the same fall in total revenue
status: Hypothetical scenario, not an estimate of reform revenue or household behaviour
note: CGT 30%, other income tax 45%; assumed reclassification shares. This is an accounting sensitivity, not evidence about the amount of shifting in Australia.

title: Observed bond yields provide context for a normal allowance
status: Observed RBA monthly series, cut at 11 November 2026
note: Nominal and indexed yields contain term/liquidity premia and are not an automatic policy allowance. Indexed-bond yield is not ex-post realised saving return.

title: Inflation has varied materially across Australia’s CGT history
status: Observed quarterly headline CPI inflation, ABS series republished by RBA
note: Dashed 2.5% is the model assumption, not a forecast. Inflation indexation and an interest-rate allowance answer different questions.
